summary:
Nigeria has confirmed a new Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory, twelve years after the country was declared free of the disease following an outbreak that killed eight people. The airport authority said it was working with health agencies to support containment efforts and was stepping up surveillance at airports. Uganda's health ministry said it had no confirmed active Ebola cases as of its statement.

A drone strike on a market in Abyei, a border region disputed by Sudan and South Sudan, killed at least 153 people, a local official said on Tuesday. Yohanna Akol Ngor, the Abyei administration's caretaker information minister, blamed Sudan's military, and the strike hit a nearby fuel depot. In Yemen, three Houthi missiles hit a training camp in government-controlled Shabwa province on Monday, killing 73 security recruits, according to local authorities.

Voters in Alberta overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin leaving Canada in a referendum that asked whether residents wished to remain or hold another vote on breaking away. The result is a victory for Prime Minister Mark Carney, who campaigned hard and promised a pipeline in the province. Separatists have vowed to fight on.

headlines.title: US envoy Witkoff meets Putin in Russia after talks with Zelenskyy
headlines.summary: US envoy Witkoff is in Russia for talks with Vladimir Putin, after what Secretary of State Marco Rubio called 'positive' talks with Zelenskyy. Russian state media said the meeting is taking place at the Konstantinovsky Palace in Saint Petersburg.

headlines.title: UK government approves Jackdaw gasfield in North Sea
headlines.summary: The UK government has approved the Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea after lobbying by Shell. The government said gas will reach homes and businesses from the end of the month, while environmental groups condemned the decision.

headlines.title: Drone strike on Abyei market kills at least 153
headlines.summary: A drone strike on a market in the disputed Abyei border region killed at least 153 people, a local official said, and hit a nearby fuel depot. South Sudanese officials blamed Sudan's military, and Doctors Without Borders said it was treating 20 wounded people.

headlines.title: Houthi missiles kill 73 security recruits in Yemen
headlines.summary: Three Houthi missiles hit a training camp in government-controlled Shabwa province on Monday, killing 73 security recruits, local authorities said. The Yemeni army said the camp was being used as a training centre.

headlines.title: Alberta voters reject leaving Canada in separatism referendum
headlines.summary: Alberta voters overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin leaving Canada, in a referendum asking whether to remain or hold another vote on breaking away. The result was a victory for Prime Minister Mark Carney, who had promised a pipeline and campaigned hard.

headlines.title: Independent MP Helen Haines loses both legs after alleged attack
headlines.summary: Independent MP Helen Haines has had both legs amputated after she was struck by a car on Monday in an alleged attack, her husband Phil Haines said. Her alleged attacker, Brendan Nugent, 43, faces multiple charges and was refused bail.
